summary.en: Keep both endpoints so insertion and removal need only local link changes.
summary.bn: দুই প্রান্তের pointer রাখলে কিউতে মান যোগ ও সরাতে পাশের link বদলালেই চলে।

notes: Programs use C17 with explicit bounds and ownership checks.

examples.title: Serve linked nodes in arrival order
examples.explanationHtml: The head leaves first while rear stays on the last node until the final removal.

examples.title: Drain, then enqueue again
examples.explanationHtml: Draining sets both endpoints to NULL; the next insertion creates a valid singleton containing 77.

examples.title: Consume a queue while summing
examples.explanationHtml: The total is six, and each serviced node is released.

practice.title: Serve and release a linked queue
practice.statementHtml: Read size 0..16 and values -99..99. Print the prompt and Served: followed by FIFO order. Free each removed node.
hints: Append using rear and remove using front.

practice.title: Count negative arrivals during service
practice.statementHtml: Read size 0..16 and values -99..99. Print the size prompt then Result: and the number of negative serviced values. Release the entire queue.
hints: Inspect the returned value before the next dequeue.

practice.title: Drain a queue and safely reuse its endpoints
practice.statementHtml: Read 0..16 values -99..99 after their count. Print the size prompt. Drain and release all nodes, enqueue 77, then print Served: 77 while releasing that last node.
hints: Final removal must clear rear before another enqueue.

practice.title: Sum serviced linked values
practice.statementHtml: Read 0..16 values -99..99 after their count. Print the size prompt and Result: with their sum while releasing the whole queue.
hints: The dequeued payload remains valid after its node is freed.

quiz.prompt: Where is a new linked queue node appended?
What are both endpoints after final removal?
quiz.explanation: The empty-state invariant covers both pointers.

quiz.prompt: What does the first enqueue set?
quiz.explanation: A singleton is both oldest and newest.

quiz.prompt: When may enqueue publish its newly allocated node?
options: Only after the queue is sorted
quiz.explanation: The old queue must remain valid on failure.

quiz.prompt: What is the next link of a newly appended tail?
quiz.explanation: The list remains an acyclic forward chain.

quiz.prompt: What extra cost comes from storing only front?
quiz.explanation: The final node is otherwise reached by traversal.

quiz.prompt: Which caller action prevents leaks when later input fails?
quiz.explanation: Losing the head loses access to every allocated node.

quiz.prompt: Which endpoint value does a two-node FIFO serve?
quiz.explanation: The first arrival is at the front.

quiz.prompt: How many non-null endpoints remain after setting both empty?
When front becomes NULL, which singleton repair condition succeeds?
quiz.explanation: The empty front tells dequeue to clear rear.

keyPoints.en: Front identifies the oldest linked queue node.
keyPoints.bn: Linked কিউতে front সবচেয়ে পুরোনো node দেখায়।

keyPoints.en: Rear makes appending possible without scanning.
keyPoints.bn: Rear থাকলে না খুঁজেই শেষে node যোগ করা যায়।

keyPoints.en: An empty linked queue has both endpoints NULL.
keyPoints.bn: Linked কিউ খালি হলে দুই endpoint-ই NULL।

keyPoints.en: The last removal clears rear before its node is freed.
keyPoints.bn: শেষ node সরানোর সময় rear-ও খালি করো।

keyPoints.en: Each successful enqueue owns one newly allocated node.
keyPoints.bn: সফল enqueue-তে কিউ একটি নতুন node-এর মালিক হয়।

examQuestions.question: Write the endpoint changes when enqueue creates the first linked node.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
node->next = NULL;
queue->front = node;
queue->rear = node;

Initialize value first and execute only after allocation succeeds. The singleton is both oldest and newest.

examQuestions.question: A linked dequeue advances front and frees old, but never changes rear. Explain the final-removal bug and repair it.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
queue->front = old->next;
if (queue->front == NULL) {
    queue->rear = NULL;
}
free(old);

Rear otherwise points to freed storage after the only node leaves. A later enqueue might write through that invalid pointer.

examQuestions.question: Explain why enqueue is O(n) with only a singly linked head and O(1) link work with front and rear.
examQuestions.answerHtml: A head-only queue must follow every next pointer to find the final node before appending. A saved rear already identifies that node. Updating rear after every append preserves constant link work. Dequeue still uses front, and final removal must clear rear. Node allocation cost is separate from pointer-update complexity.
